newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 24.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- ASEAN foreign ministers have agreed to resume a mediatory role in resolving the crisis in Cambodia but remain firm in their decision to delay the troubled country's membership in the grouping. The decision comes after Cambodia's Second Prime Minister Hun Sen rescinded last week's refusal to let the ASEAN mediate in a resolution of the conflict between the current Cambodian power broker and his rival, ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Sihanouk. (THE NATION, BANGKOK POST)

- More than 20,000 refugees from fighting in Cambodia are poised to seek sanctuary across the border. Refugees in O-Samet have been short of food since the closure of Chong Chom pass in Kab Choeng district, and others fleeing fighting in Samrong are heading for the border. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Constitution Scrutiny Committee has agreed in principle to let senators initiate legislation but not serve in the cabinet unless they have been out of the Upper House for at least two years. The committee has looked over details of senate-related articles with an adhoc panel it appointed to deal with issues concerning senators. (BANGKOK POST)

- The baht plunged to a new low of 32.50 against the U.S. dollar yesterday amid widespread fears that the currency will head further downhill when the details of finance companies' non-performing loans are announced today. Dealers say they expect the baht to hit another record low of between 33 baht to 35 baht to the dollar within the next week. (THE NATION, BUSINESS DAY)

- The Finance Ministry is studying new steps, which are being kept secret for now, to aid the recovery of economy since the depreciation of the baht. Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya has told the International Monetary Fund that the measures have to be finalised before discussions are held with the agency. (BANGKOK POST)
